analysis.note: Nañ-tatpuruṣa/prefixal negative formation; present-participial second member from √ej, used adjectivally of the neuter ātmatattva.

verification.detail: compound stem anejat as Napumsaka/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Neuter nominative singular agreeing with the implicit neuter ātmatattva/tat.
Ablative of comparison with javīyaḥ: ‘swifter than the mind.’
Comparative adjective, neuter nominative singular, agreeing with the ātmatattva.
Object of āpnuvan; final -t is voiced before devāḥ in the printed saṃhitā.
Śaṅkara takes these ‘shining ones’ as the senses beginning with sight, not as independent gods in the ordinary mythological sense.
Vedic imperfect, 3rd plural parasmaipada in sense ‘reached/attained’; negated by na.

Corrected from a finite Laṅ analysis: finite Laṅ from √ṛṣ would give ārṣat/ārṣad, while the printed arṣat is the neuter nominative singular present-participial form, here used predicatively and glossed by Śaṅkara as pūrvam eva gataṃ, ‘already gone before.’
Neuter nominative singular subject of atyeti, referring to the ātmatattva.
Accusative plural masculine present participle agreeing with anyān: ‘the others as running.’
Object of atyeti, explained as mind, speech, senses, etc., distinct from the Self.
Present 3rd singular: ‘passes beyond, outstrips.’ The lemma is cited by bare root √i with prefix ati by convention.
Neuter nominative singular present-participial stem from √sthā, agreeing with tat: ‘standing/still.’
Locative singular referring to the ātmatattva as the ever-conscious basis.
Morphologically the familiar feminine accusative plural form; Śaṅkara interprets the word here as karmāṇi, ‘actions/activities,’ not waters.
A lexical name; Śaṅkara identifies it with vāyu, the activity-principle bearing all prāṇas.
Present 3rd singular: Śaṅkara primarily glosses ‘apportions/distributes’ (vibhajati), with an alternative ‘sustains’ (dhārayati).

justifications.decision: anejat is not a separate finite clause ‘it does not move’ but a neuter adjectival negative formation meaning ‘unmoving,’ and ekaṃ marks the same one ātman present in all beings.
options_considered: anejat as a finite verbal negation: ‘it does not move’
anejat as an adjectival nañ-formation: ‘unmoving’
ekaṃ as a bare numeral only
ekaṃ as ‘one and the same’ of the ātman in all beings
justifications.chosen: Read anejat as ‘unmoving,’ the privative of ejat ‘moving/shaking,’ and ekaṃ as ‘one’ with reference to the single ātmatattva in all beings.

evidence.quote: anejat na ejat / ejṛ kampane, kampanaṃ calanaṃ svāvasthāpracyutistadvarjitaṃ sarvadaikarūpamityarthaḥ /
evidence.translation: ‘anejat’ means ‘not ejat’; √ej is shaking, and shaking is motion, a lapse from one’s own state; the meaning is that it is devoid of that and always of one form.
And that is one in all beings.

justifications.decision: The apparent contradiction between ‘unmoving’ and ‘swifter than mind’ is resolved by Śaṅkara through the distinction between the unconditioned Self and its appearance with limiting adjuncts.
options_considered: Take the mantra as ascribing literal motion and stillness simultaneously
Take ‘swifter than mind’ figuratively, relative to the mind-upādhi, while the Self itself remains changeless
justifications.chosen: Translate both predicates, but understand the speed-predicate as due to mental upādhi and apparent manifestation, not real change in the Self.

evidence.quote: kathaṃ viruddhamucyate dhruvaṃ niścalamidaṃ manaso javīya iti ca / naiṣa doṣaḥ / nirupādhyupādhimattvenopapatteḥ
evidence.translation: Objection: how can the fixed and motionless be called swifter than mind? This is no fault, because it is intelligible as unconditioned and as possessed of limiting adjuncts.

evidence.quote: manaso 'ntaḥkaraṇasya saṅkalpavikalpalakṣaṇasyopādheranuvarttanād ... tasmin manasi brahmalokādīn drutaṃ gacchati sati prathamaṃ prāpta ivātmacaitanyāvabhāso gṛhyate 'to manaso javīya ityāha /
evidence.translation: Because it follows the upādhi, the internal organ called mind, characterized by resolve and doubt; when that mind goes swiftly even to Brahmaloka and the like, the manifestation of Self-consciousness is grasped as though it had arrived first—therefore the text says ‘swifter than mind.’

justifications.decision: manasaḥ is an ablative of comparison with javīyaḥ, and ‘mind’ is specifically the saṅkalpa/vikalpa-type internal organ.
options_considered: Genitive: ‘the mind’s swifter one’
Ablative: ‘swifter than the mind’
manas as a vague soul/spirit
manas as the antaḥkaraṇa characterized by saṅkalpa-vikalpa
justifications.chosen: Read ‘manaso javīyaḥ’ as ‘swifter than the mind,’ where mind is the internal organ of ideation.

evidence.translation: ‘Swifter than the mind’—than mind characterized by resolve and the like; more possessed of speed.
The mind is the internal organ characterized by resolve and doubt.

justifications.decision: devāḥ here are not translated simply as mythic gods; Śaṅkara identifies them as the luminous sense-faculties, eye and the rest, which cannot attain the Self.
options_considered: devāḥ as gods/deities in general
devāḥ as the sense-faculties because of their illuminating function
justifications.chosen: Translate as ‘deva-s, the shining senses,’ and take enat as the already introduced Self-principle which they do not reach.

evidence.quote: nainaddevā dyotanāddevāścakṣurādīnīndriyāṇyetatprakṛtamātmatattvaṃ nāpnuvanna prāptavantaḥ / tebhyo mano javīyaḥ manovyāpāravyavahitatvād ābhāsamātramapi ātmano naiva devānāṃ viṣayībhavati /
evidence.translation: The deva-s are so called from shining: the sense-organs beginning with the eye. They did not attain this Self-principle under discussion. Since mind is swifter than they, and since the operation of mind intervenes, not even a mere appearance of the Self becomes an object for the deva-s.

justifications.decision: pūrvam arṣat is a participial predication of the Self: ‘already gone before,’ grounded in the Self’s all-pervasiveness, not a finite Laṅ form.
options_considered: arṣat as a finite Laṅ verb ‘went/sped’
arṣat as a neuter nominative singular present-participial form used predicatively
pūrvam as spatially eastern/front only
pūrvam as temporally/priorly ‘beforehand’
justifications.chosen: Read arṣat morphologically as a neuter nominative singular participial form from √ṛṣ; in context, with Śaṅkara’s gloss, translate the predication as ‘already gone before.’

evidence.quote: yasmājjavanānmanaso 'pi pūrvamarṣat pūrvameva gataṃ vyomavadvyāpitvāt sarvavyāpi tadātmatattva
evidence.translation: Because, even before the swift mind, it was ‘arṣat’—already gone before—since, like space, it is all-pervasive; that Self-principle is all-pervasive.

justifications.decision: dhāvataḥ anyān is accusative plural: the ‘other’ runners are mind, speech, senses, etc.; atyeti is qualified by Śaṅkara’s iva because the Self itself remains stationary.
options_considered: dhāvataḥ as genitive singular: ‘of the running one’
dhāvataḥ as accusative plural agreeing with anyān: ‘the running others’
atyeti as literal locomotion by the Self
atyeti as ‘outstrips, as it were,’ while the Self stands changeless
justifications.chosen: Read ‘tat dhāvataḥ anyān atyeti tiṣṭhat’ as: ‘That, while standing, as it were outstrips the other runners.’

evidence.quote: taddhāvato drutaṃ gacchato 'nyānātmavilakṣaṇānmanovāgindriyaprabhṛtīnatyeti atītya gacchati iva / ivārthaṃ svayameva darśayati tiṣṭhaditi svayamavikriyameva sadityarthaḥ /
evidence.translation: ‘That outstrips the running others,’ those unlike the Self—mind, speech, senses, and the like—who go swiftly; it goes beyond, as it were. The word ‘standing’ itself shows the sense ‘as it were’: the meaning is that it itself remains changeless.

justifications.decision: tasmin is the Self-principle as the ever-conscious basis; mātariśvā is Vāyu/prāṇa; apaḥ means actions or activities, not waters; dadhāti is primarily ‘apportions/distributes,’ with ‘sustains’ as an allowed alternative.
options_considered: tasmin as a merely spatial ‘in that object’
tasmin as the ever-conscious ātmatattva serving as basis
mātariśvā as Agni or a mythic figure only
mātariśvā as vāyu, bearer of all prāṇas and activity-principle
apaḥ as literal waters
apaḥ as karmāṇi, activities
dadhāti as places only
dadhāti as apportions/distributes; alternatively sustains
justifications.chosen: Translate: ‘In that, Mātariśvan apportions the actions,’ understanding Mātariśvan as Vāyu/prāṇa and apaḥ as activities.

evidence.quote: tasminnātmatattve sati nityacaitanyasvabhāve mātariśvā vāyuḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛt kriyātmako
evidence.translation: In that Self-principle, whose nature is eternal consciousness, Mātariśvan is Vāyu, the bearer of all prāṇas, of the nature of activity.

evidence.quote: apaḥ karmāṇi prāṇināṃ ceṣṭālakṣaṇāni, agnyādityaparjanyādīnāṃ jvalanadahanaprakāśābhivarṣaṇādilakṣaṇāni dadhāti vibhajati ityarthaḥ /
evidence.translation: ‘apaḥ’ means actions: the motions of living beings and the burning, consuming, shining, raining, and similar functions of fire, sun, rain-cloud, and so on. ‘dadhāti’ means ‘apportions/distributes.’

evidence.quote: sarvā hi kāryakaraṇādivikriyā nityacaitanyātmasvarūpe sarvāspadabhūte satyeva bhavantītyarthaḥ
evidence.translation: All transformations of effects, instruments, and so forth occur only when the Self whose nature is eternal consciousness exists as the basis of all.

translation:
Unmoving, one, swifter than the mind—
the deva-s, the shining senses, did not reach this,
already gone before.

That, standing still, outstrips as it were
the others as they run.
In that Self-principle, Mātariśvan, the wind/prāṇa,
apportions the actions (apaḥ).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation would likely render devāḥ simply as ‘gods’; Śaṅkara instead identifies them with the illuminating sense-faculties such as the eye.
It would likely translate apaḥ as ‘waters’; Śaṅkara explicitly glosses it as karmāṇi, the activities/functions of living beings and cosmic powers.
It might take the verse as asserting real motion of the Self; Śaṅkara repeatedly insists that the motion is only apparent through upādhi, while the Self is svayam avikriya, changeless in itself.
It might miss that manasaḥ is ablative of comparison and that ‘mind’ means the saṅkalpa-vikalpa-type antaḥkaraṇa.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented anejat as an + ejat and cited ejat; this apparatus treats the printed word as a single nañ-tatpuruṣa/adjectival stem anejat, because the mūla has one word and Śaṅkara glosses ‘anejat na ejat’ (lines 1–2).

ByT5’s canonical lemma for dhāvataḥ was sarat; this apparatus uses the form-deriving participial stem dhāvat from √dhāv, supported by the surface form and Śaṅkara’s gloss ‘dhāvato drutaṃ gacchataḥ’ (line 11).
open_questions: The commentary file is explicitly unproofread; avoided relying on visibly noisy printed material where not needed. The line-13 word printed as vighārayitṛ appears suspect in context, but no argument here depends on that reading.
apaḥ is morphologically the common feminine accusative plural form of ap; Śaṅkara’s semantic gloss karmāṇi is followed for translation even though the gloss-word is neuter plural.
mula: anejad ekaṃ manaso javīyo nainaddevā āpnuvanpūrvamarṣat | taddhāvato 'nyānatyeti tiṣṭhat tasminn apo mātariśvā dadhāti
commentary_lines: ejṛ kampane, kampanaṃ calanaṃ svāvasthāpracyutistadvarjitaṃ sarvadaikarūpamityarthaḥ /
taccaikaṃ sarvabhūteṣu manasaḥ saṅkalpādilakṣaṇād javīyo javavattaram /
kathaṃ viruddhamucyate dhruvaṃ niścalamidaṃ manaso javīya iti ca /

nirupādhyupādhimattvenopapatteḥ tatra nirupādhikena svena rūpeṇocyate anejadekamiti manaso 'ntaḥkaraṇasya saṅkalpavikalpalakṣaṇasyopādheranuvarttanād iha dehasthasya manaso brahmalokādidūragamanaṃ saṅkalpena kṣaṇamātrādbhavatītyato manaso javiṣṭhatvaṃ loke prasiddham /
tasmin manasi brahmalokādīn drutaṃ gacchati sati prathamaṃ prāpta ivātmacaitanyāvabhāso gṛhyate 'to manaso javīya ityāha /
tebhyo mano javīyaḥ manovyāpāravyavahitatvād ābhāsamātramapi ātmano naiva devānāṃ viṣayībhavati /

yasmājjavanānmanaso 'pi pūrvamarṣat pūrvameva gataṃ vyomavadvyāpitvāt sarvavyāpi tadātmatattva sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjitaṃ svena nirupādhikena svarūpeṇāvikriyameva sadupādhikṛtāḥ sarvāḥ saṃsāravikriyā anubhavatītyavivekināṃ mūḍhānāmanekamiva ca pratidehaṃ pratyavabhāsata ityetadāha /
taddhāvato drutaṃ gacchato 'nyānātmavilakṣaṇānmanovāgindriyaprabhṛtīnatyeti atītya gacchati iva /
ivārthaṃ svayameva darśayati tiṣṭhaditi svayamavikriyameva sadityarthaḥ /

tasminnātmatattve sati nityacaitanyasvabhāve mātariśvā vāyuḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛt kriyātmako yadāśrayāṇi kāryakaraṇajātāni yasminnotāni protāni ca yatsūtrasaṃjñakaṃ sarvasya jagato vighārayitṛ sa mātariśvā; apaḥ karmāṇi prāṇināṃ ceṣṭālakṣaṇāni, agnyādityaparjanyādīnāṃ jvalanadahanaprakāśābhivarṣaṇādilakṣaṇāni dadhāti vibhajati ityarthaḥ /
sarvā hi kāryakaraṇādivikriyā nityacaitanyātmasvarūpe sarvāspadabhūte satyeva bhavantītyarthaḥ
